bundle.name: Spain on foot
bundle.description: Eight day-shaped walks across Spain's best trails, each with the right trailhead, the right direction and the meal that belongs at the end of it.

playbooks.name: Cares Gorge, walked from Poncebos so the climb comes first
playbooks.summary: The 12 km canal path into Cain and back, done in the only direction that makes sense, with cabrito at the far end.

sourceTrip.name: Asturias and the Picos, on foot

stops.title: First car down the AS-264 to Poncebos

location.name: Puente de Poncebos riverside car park

stops.notes: The road in is single-track with passing places; after 08:30 you meet the tour minibuses head-on and reverse a lot. Park at the lower riverside lot, not the upper one, which belongs to the Bulnes funicular.

stops.title: Cafe con leche at Hotel Garganta del Cares
stops.notes: Last real coffee for 12 km. Fill both bottles here: there is one spring on the whole trail and it is eight kilometres in, on the Cain side.

stops.title: Poncebos to Cain along the canal path, 12 km
stops.notes: This is the whole trick: walk north to south. From Poncebos you get the brutal 300 m of Camarmena zig-zags done in cool shade in the first hour and everything after is flat. Start from Cain and you finish with that climb at four in the afternoon in full sun. The morning light is behind you this way too.

stops.title: Cabrito asado at Casa Cuevas in Cain
stops.notes: Fourth place on the left walking up from the river into the village. Order the cabrito asado, and have the Cabrales with cider rather than wine - the cheese is made in the valley you just walked out of.

stops.title: Cold dip at the Cain footbridge

location.name: Rio Cares footbridge below the village

stops.notes: Snowmelt, so about eight degrees in May and worth exactly ninety seconds. Nobody regrets it on the walk back.

stops.title: Back to Poncebos before the wind gets up
stops.notes: The return is roughly 45 minutes quicker and finishes downhill. Afternoon wind funnels up the gorge from about three; the tunnels are the only shelter and there is no phone signal between them.

stops.title: Cabrales cheese cave at Arenas
stops.notes: A 25-minute guided walk into the limestone cave where the cheese matures. Last entry is five, and it is the only thing open between finishing the walk and dinner.

playbooks.name: Fuente De: ride the cable car up and never take it back down
playbooks.summary: One-way ticket to El Cable, lentils at Cabana Veronica, then 1,200 m of descent through the Puertos de Aliva to Espinama.

sourceTrip.name: Cantabria: the Picos from the south

stops.title: Potes to Fuente De for the first cabin

location.name: Teleferico de Fuente De lower station

stops.notes: The station car park is full by 09:30 in July. The queue for tickets is far longer than the queue for the cabin, so send one person ahead while the others sort boots.

stops.title: One-way ticket up the teleferico

location.name: Teleferico de Fuente De ticket hall

stops.notes: Buy the single, not the return - you are walking down the other side. 753 metres of ascent in under four minutes; stand on the left of the cabin for the wall.

stops.title: El Cable to Cabana Veronica by the Horcados Rojos track

location.name: Mirador de El Cable, PR-PNPE 23 trailhead

stops.notes: A limestone desert with no water, no shade and no soil. The route is cairned rather than signed, so in cloud you follow the jeep track to the Horcados junction instead of cutting the moraine.

stops.title: Lentils at Cabana Veronica
stops.notes: An aircraft-carrier gun turret bolted to the rock at 2,325 m, sleeping twelve. The guardian cooks one pot of lentejas a day for whoever turns up. Cash only, no card, no signal.

stops.title: Scramble to the Horcados Rojos col
stops.notes: Thirty minutes above the hut and the only point on this route where you see the Naranjo de Bulnes head-on. Skip it in cloud - there is nothing to see and the scree is loose.

stops.title: Down the Puertos de Aliva to Espinama
stops.notes: A long, kind 1,200 m descent past the Chalet Real and the summer cattle. Poles earn their place in the final hour, which is concrete track rather than path.

stops.title: Cocido lebaniego at Hotel Remona
stops.notes: First building you reach walking into Espinama. Cocido lebaniego is the chickpea stew of this valley and it arrives in three courses, so order one between two if you still have driving to do.

stops.title: Taxi back up to the car at Fuente De
stops.notes: Four kilometres uphill on the CA-185. There is no rank - ring from the hotel before you sit down to eat, not after, because one driver covers the whole valley.

playbooks.name: Caminito del Rey: park at the finish, walk it downhill
playbooks.summary: The boardwalks one-way from the Ardales gate to El Chorro, with the shuttle taken first instead of last.

stops.title: Park at El Chorro station and take the shuttle north

location.name: El Chorro-Caminito del Rey railway station

stops.notes: Park at the finish, not the start. The shuttle runs El Chorro to the north entrance every half hour, costs 2.50 euros and is cash only - no cards, no notes over twenty. Doing it this way means the walk ends where the car is instead of with an hour of waiting.

stops.title: Tostada at El Kiosko before the gate
stops.notes: The last food, water and toilet before the boardwalk - nothing is sold on the walk itself. Leave 25 minutes after this for the access path and tunnel to the control point; your slot is timed at the gate, not the car park.

stops.title: Control point: named ticket and helmet

location.name: Caminito del Rey north control gate

stops.notes: Ten euros general admission, eighteen with an official guide, booked on caminitodelrey.info. Tickets are personalised after purchase and the name has to match the passport you hand over - they do check. Helmets are issued here and worn the whole way.

stops.title: The boardwalks: Gaitanejo gorge to the hanging bridge
stops.notes: 7.7 km end to end including access paths, one-way north to south and downhill throughout. The glass floor panel and the suspension bridge are both in the last third, so nobody bails early. Wind closes this walk far more often than rain does - ring the visitor centre the morning of, not the night before.

stops.title: Terrace lunch at La Garganta
stops.notes: Beside the station at the south exit, with the gorge you just walked as the backdrop. Book it - every slot for two hours comes out of the same gate at the same time and the terrace fills in ten minutes.

stops.title: Drive up to the Conde de Guadalhorce reservoir

location.name: Mirador del Embalse del Conde de Guadalhorce

stops.notes: Ten minutes north on the MA-5403. In February it is a view and a coffee; in July it is the swim that makes the whole day.

playbooks.name: GR221 Deia to Port de Soller, with the Cala Deia detour done early
playbooks.summary: The best stage of the dry-stone route walked toward the sea, dropping into the cove before the crowd and finishing on the tram.

sourceTrip.name: Tramuntana in March, before the heat

stops.title: Bus 203 out to Deia

location.name: Soller bus stop, Carrer de Cetre

stops.notes: Ride the bus at the start of the day, not the end. Walking the stage north-east means you finish at the sea in Port de Soller with a tram home, instead of standing at a Deia roadside at six with everyone else.

stops.title: Coffee in the Deia square before dropping to the sea

location.name: Placa de Deia, below Sa Fonda

stops.notes: Refugi Can Boi, the GR221 stage hut, is two minutes below the square if you are doing the route in stages - twenty-odd beds, booked through the Consell de Mallorca months ahead, never on the day.

stops.title: Down the cobbles to Cala Deia
stops.notes: Thirty minutes down through olive terraces on a stepped cobbled path. Go now: the cove is empty before eleven and the water is glass. Ca's Patro March, the fish shack on the rocks, only opens for lunch from about one, so it is a reason to come back rather than a reason to wait.

stops.title: First swim of the trip
stops.notes: March water is around fifteen degrees and the shingle is punishing barefoot - the sandals are worth carrying for exactly this.

stops.title: Back up to the GR221 and on over Llucalcari

location.name: GR221 Ruta de Pedra en Sec, Deia to Muleta section

stops.notes: The climb out of the cala is the only real work of the day: 200 m in 25 minutes. After Llucalcari the path traverses high above the sea for two hours with no shade and no water, so carry two litres. Both places people go wrong are at the Llucalcari houses - keep the sea on your left and look for the red-and-white flash painted on the dry-stone wall.

stops.title: Refugi Muleta and the Cap Gros lighthouse
stops.notes: The old army telegraph station, in use until 1956, now a forty-bed refugi. Its terrace is where the whole bay opens up in one go - the best five minutes of the stage and most people walk straight past it.

stops.title: Late lunch on the Repic waterfront
stops.notes: The path drops you at the far, lighthouse end of the bay; the restaurants are twenty minutes round the water. Kitchens here stop at four sharp, which is the real reason not to linger at Muleta.

stops.title: Wooden tram back to Soller

location.name: Tranvia de Soller, Port de Soller terminus

stops.notes: Runs every half hour through the orange groves to Soller station, tickets bought on board. Sit on the right for the groves, stand on the back platform if it is full.

playbooks.name: Ordesa the right way round: up the Cazadores, home along the Faja de Pelay
playbooks.summary: A guided full circuit of the Ordesa canyon - 800 m of climb before the sun, three level hours on a cliff ledge, and lamb in Torla.

stops.title: First shuttle from Torla into the valley
stops.notes: The valley road is closed to private cars from 19 June to 20 September and on the shoulder-season weekends listed on the park site. The shuttle is six euros return; it runs every fifteen to twenty minutes from eight, but only every half hour before that. Take the 06:45 - you want the Cazadores climb finished before the sun reaches the wall.

stops.title: Meet the guide at Pradera de Ordesa
stops.notes: An AEGM mountain guide for the day, split four ways. Worth paying for on this route specifically: the Cazadores has an exposed ladder-and-chain section near the top, and the weather over Monte Perdido turns by lunchtime far more often than the forecast admits.

stops.title: Senda de los Cazadores: 800 m straight up
stops.notes: Unrelenting - 800 m of switchbacks in two and a half kilometres, in beech shade the whole way. Walk it UP and never down: the Faja is the reward and it has to come second, and the loose upper section is genuinely unpleasant descending.

stops.title: Mirador de Calcilarruego
stops.notes: The balcony where the canyon suddenly drops 700 m below your boots. This is where the day stops being work and starts being a walk - sit down, eat something, everyone does.

stops.title: Faja de Pelay: three flat hours on a ledge
stops.notes: A natural terrace cut across the cliff face, almost dead level, with the whole canyon open on your right and the Cotatuero waterfalls opposite. No water and no shade for three hours - this is where the two litres go.

stops.title: Picnic below the Cola de Caballo

location.name: Circo de Soaso, Cola de Caballo falls

stops.notes: Buy the bocadillos at the Torla bakery the night before - the Pradera kiosk opens at nine, which is too late for this itinerary. Refugio de Goriz is 45 minutes further up and sells soup, but beds there are booked out months ahead and day walkers get short shrift.

stops.title: Valley floor home past the Gradas de Soaso

location.name: Camino del Valle, Gradas de Soaso

stops.notes: Easy river path with the stepped cascades the whole way down. Two hours if you push, three if you swim in the pools below the Gradas. Last shuttle out of the Pradera is seven in high season and it is a nine-kilometre road walk if you miss it.

stops.title: Ternasco at El Duende
stops.notes: A dozen tables in a stone house off the main street. Ring at breakfast to hold one; by the time you walk out of the park it is gone. Roast ternasco - Aragonese milk-fed lamb - is the thing here.

playbooks.name: Teide: the first cable car, the paid permit, and the last 163 metres
playbooks.summary: Spain's highest point on the Telesforo Bravo permit, with the 2026 fee, the altitude problem and the only decent lunch in the park.

stops.title: Up the TF-21 through the cloud sea
stops.notes: Leave before seven and you climb out through the mar de nubes at sunrise, which is half the reason to do this from the north side. There is no fuel inside the park - fill up in La Orotava, not Vilaflor.

stops.title: Coffee at the Parador before anything opens

location.name: Parador de Las Canadas del Teide

stops.notes: The only building for miles and the terrace looks straight across at the Roques de Garcia. It is also the last warm room before 3,555 m: it is often five degrees at the top station in October with wind on top of that.

stops.title: Cable car up to La Rambleta
stops.notes: Book the earliest slot at volcanoteide.com. The cable car stops running when wind at the top passes about sixty km/h, and afternoons are reliably windier than mornings - the first departure is the one that actually goes.

stops.title: Show the Telesforo Bravo permit at 3,555 m

location.name: La Rambleta permit control, PNT-10 gate

stops.notes: The summit permit stopped being free in 2026: fifteen euros for non-residents, six for other Canary residents, free for Tenerife residents and under-14s, booked on the TenerifeON platform. New places are released every Monday at 07:00 Canary time, 56 days out, and they go in minutes. The permit covers a two-hour window and the ranger checks the passport against the name.

stops.title: Sendero Telesforo Bravo to the crater rim
stops.notes: Only 163 m of climb to 3,715 m, but at this altitude it still takes an hour. The sulphur vents at the rim are hot enough to burn a hand. Half the people up here get a headache: walk absurdly slowly, drink before you feel thirsty, and turn around if it gets worse rather than better.

stops.title: Cable car down before the queue builds
stops.notes: The queue at the top station is worse than the one at the bottom and gets ugly after noon. If you would rather walk, hand back the return leg and take PNT-07 down to Montana Blanca - 1,200 m of loose pumice, about three hours, and it only works if you left a second car at the Montana Blanca gate on the TF-21.

stops.title: Puchero at the Parador's Restaurante El Refugio

location.name: Restaurante El Refugio, Parador de Las Canadas del Teide

stops.notes: The only proper meal inside the park boundary. Ask for a terrace table facing the Roques and order the conejo en salmorejo or the puchero canario; the papas arrugadas come with both mojos.

stops.title: Bizcochon and coffee at Casa Egon
stops.notes: A 1916 pastry shop with a courtyard behind it. The drive down from 2,100 m to sea level takes 45 minutes and your ears will pop twice - this is the right place to stop while your head resettles.

playbooks.name: Garganta Verde on the free permit, then three white villages
playbooks.summary: A 400 m descent into a vulture gorge that is closed all summer, followed by Zahara's castle and dinner in Grazalema.

stops.title: The CA-9104 over the pass to the trailhead

location.name: Sendero Garganta Verde trailhead lay-by, CA-9104

stops.notes: The lay-by holds maybe fifteen cars and there is nowhere else to leave one. The Grazalema-Zahara pass is the best drive in Andalucia and it is worth doing early for the light on Zahara's castle rock.

stops.title: Show the Junta de Andalucia permit at the gate
stops.notes: Free, but compulsory and genuinely enforced. Request it up to two months ahead through the Ventana del Visitante site; a PDF arrives by email and the forest guard reads it off your phone. The trail is closed 1 June to 15 October for griffon vulture nesting, which is what makes this a winter and spring walk rather than a summer one.

stops.title: Down into the gorge to the Ermita cave
stops.notes: Two and a half kilometres down, 400 m of descent, and every metre of it has to be climbed back out - budget the return at twice the descent. The griffon colony nests on the walls above and you hear them before you see them. The 'Ermita' at the bottom is a travertine cave the size of a chapel.

stops.title: Mirador de los Buitres on the way out
stops.notes: Five minutes off the path near the rim. At midday the vultures ride the thermals level with your head and close enough to hear the primaries.

stops.title: Lunch above the reservoir at Al Lago
stops.notes: Terrace over the turquoise embalse at the bottom of the village. Closed Mondays and it shortens its hours in deep winter, so ring the same morning. Ask for the lower terrace.

stops.title: Up to Zahara's Nasrid keep

location.name: Torre del Homenaje, Castillo de Zahara

stops.notes: Twenty minutes of steps up from the church, free, and the only spot where the reservoir and the Pinsapar ridge sit in the same frame.

stops.title: The blanket mill at Grazalema
stops.notes: The last working wool mill in the sierra, on the edge of the village. Blankets run roughly ninety to a hundred and forty euros. Grazalema is the wettest place in Spain, which is exactly why the pinsapo firs and the wool trade are both here.

stops.title: Dinner at Cadiz El Chico

location.name: Restaurante Cadiz El Chico, Plaza de Espana

stops.notes: On the plaza and the only serious kitchen in the village, so book. Sopa de tomate grazalemena first, then the payoyo goat cheese from the farms you drove past this morning.

playbooks.name: The best day on the Camino Frances: Villafranca del Bierzo up to O Cebreiro
playbooks.summary: Twenty-eight kilometres along the Valcarce and then 700 m up a cattle track into Galicia, with the pack sent ahead.

stops.title: Stamp the credencial and hand the pack to Jacotrans
stops.notes: If you use the backpack transfer once on the whole Camino, use it today. Envelope with the cash left on the bag at the albergue before eight, and it is waiting at O Cebreiro. Seven hundred metres of climb at the end of twenty-eight kilometres is a completely different day with ten kilos on your back. Get the sello here too - the next one is twelve kilometres on.

stops.title: The valley route along the Valcarce, not the Pradela hill
stops.notes: Two waymarked options leave Villafranca. The Pradela variant climbs 300 m for a view; the valley route hugs the river under the A-6 flyovers and is shorter and flatter. Take the valley - you need the legs for O Cebreiro, and the concrete viaducts arching over a chestnut river are far stranger and better than the guidebook photos suggest. Second breakfast at Casa Susi in Trabadelo if it is open.

stops.title: Trabadelo to Herrerias past the Castillo de Sarracin

location.name: Camino Frances via Vega de Valcarce

stops.notes: Chestnut woods, a ruined ninth-century castle on the hill above Vega, and the last flat ground you will see today. Fill water at the Vega fountain in the square.

stops.title: Eat properly at Herrerias before the climb

location.name: Herrerias village bar, by the bridge

stops.notes: This is the decision point of the day. La Faba is three and a half kilometres and 400 m straight up a stone-walled holloway with nothing in between, and after that it is another 300 m to the top. A full plate and twenty minutes off your feet here is worth an hour later.

stops.title: The climb: Herrerias, La Faba, Laguna de Castilla, O Cebreiro

location.name: Camino Frances ascent to O Cebreiro

stops.notes: Seven hundred metres of climb in eight kilometres, most of it on a sunken cattle track that is mud after rain. You cross into Galicia just past Laguna de Castilla and the first granite kilometre marker appears. In October the mist comes up the valley behind you as you climb, which is the view everybody remembers from the whole Camino.

stops.title: Bed at the Xunta albergue

location.name: Albergue de Peregrinos da Xunta de Galicia

stops.notes: Xunta albergues are first-come and cannot be reserved. Arrive by five in season or you are walking another five kilometres to Hospital da Condesa. Bring a sleeping bag: they issue a mattress and a disposable sheet, nothing warmer, and it is 1,300 m up.

stops.title: The pallozas and Santa Maria la Real

location.name: Iglesia de Santa Maria la Real

stops.notes: Ninth century and the oldest church still standing on the entire Camino Frances, with the pre-Roman thatched pallozas beside it. This is the reason to stop here rather than push on to Fonfria, and it takes twenty minutes.

stops.title: Caldo gallego at Meson Anton
stops.notes: It is cold up here in every month of the year and the caldo is the entire point. Order the queso do Cebreiro as well - cone-shaped, made in this village, and effectively unavailable anywhere else on the route.
